plaintext.source: Mikel García Larragan published a full online decipherment of AHPZ C_CRAR/000001/0024 on 16 July 2026 (El blog de García Larragan y Cía, Criptografía CCCLXXXIV). On the manuscript itself, C_CRAR/000001/0024 bears a single 1-word contemporary interlinear gloss ('y su bi vn gia' above L21 tokens 9-15), while sibling AHPZ C_CRAR/000001/0022 (15 Aug 1477) in the same file carries a complete contemporary interlinear decipherment.

transcription.source: DARA Aragón PDF AHPZ_C_CRAR_000024.pdf (https://opacaraimagenes.aragon.es/7a/9e/AHPZ_C_CRAR_000024.pdf; native 160-dpi embedded JPEGs upscaled up to 300 dpi for inspection)
transcription.notes: 63 solid cipher lines across f. 1r (L01-L31), f. 1v (L32-L60), and f. 2r (L61-L63): 1,915 space-separated tokens across 126 distinct types (IC=0.01867); audited across strips and enlarged crops by AI models only (no human check yet), with 4 model-settled scan amendments bracketed in reading_2854.md (L45 tok 13: 91 -> gi, L01 tok 20: 20 -> 10, L03 tok 17: 44 -> 45 = pi, L62 tok 17: 20 -> 10 = ci); clear framing and L21 gloss isolated in diplomatic_2854.txt.

system.summary: Four-tier Castilian-Aragonese royal cipher (key family published in Larragan 2026, Tomokiyo 2018 §2.4, and Bertomeu pp. 212-213; rebuilt here from sibling AHPZ C_CRAR/000001/0022) combining a sequential 75-slot CV-syllabary (3-77 across 15 consonants x 5 vowels, with stemless Aragonese 5, open-top ribbon gam=8, dotted ii=11), homophonic single-letter symbols, two-letter function-word codes (de/di/do/du, fa/fi/fo/fu, q_d, p_bar), and royal/territorial nomenclators (gi=Vuestra Alteza, gam2=Rey, gam4=Conde, gam6=Reyno, 95=Sicilia, 96=Cerdenya, 99=Francia).

diacritics.note: Overbars, crossbars, double bars, and dot pairs distinguish homophones and letter variants (q_bar/q_dbl, tt/tt_dot, ct/ct_dot, b_bar/b_bar_dot/b_dbl, e_tail/e_dot, gt/gt_dot, d_bar/d_bar_dot, L_dot, k_bar).

system.sibling_key: The key family was already published from BNE witnesses by Satoshi Tomokiyo (2018, §2.4) and Mikel García Larragan (incl. his 16 July 2026 decipherment of this letter). Here the key was rebuilt from same-secretary sibling AHPZ C_CRAR/000001/0022 in the same file (Medina del Campo, 15 Aug 1477, J. Arinyo secr., Ansorena 2017 lot 503 item 22; 24 physical cipher lines with contemporary interlinear decipherment; 95=Sicilia on L02/L06/L19 checked on crops by AI models only, not a person). AHPZ C_CRAR/000001/0020 (#2856) was reported in issue #1016 as not a cipher.

solution.what: Downloaded scans of #2854, #2855, and #2856 plus 16 neighboring AHPZ C_CRAR/000001/ PDFs (0010, 0015-0032); verified #2856 (0020) shows no cipher passage (reported in issue #1016), #2855 (0026) is an unrelated glossed Catalan cipher, and #2854 (0024) spans 63 bare cipher lines across 2.1 pages.

Located same-secretary witness AHPZ C_CRAR/000001/0022 (Medina del Campo, 15 Aug 1477, J. Arinyo secr., 24 physical cipher lines with contemporary interlinear decipherment) in the same file; rebuilt 92 direct WITNESS_CRAR22 mappings + 6 calligraphic allographs plus regular 3..77 CV-syllabary grid slots.
Transcribed all 63 cipher lines of #2854 (1,915 space-separated tokens, IC=0.01867) across f. 1r-2r, with 4 AI-model crop amendments subsequently bracketed as probable in reading_2854.md.

Validated leak-free Golden Age Spanish LM (es-golden-age-nospace) on held-out targets/ferdinand1473 synthetic control (743 chars, 38 unspaced homophonic tokens, zero overlap): 0-crib blind SA recovered 734/743 = 98.79% char accuracy (z=+46.05 vs 6 blind SA nulls, z=+21.52/+34.30 vs 200 shuffles, p=0.0050; DummyAllE=FAIL).

Resolved 1477->1478 shifted values (b_bar=s, gam2=rey), matched 95=Sicilia against CRAR_22 L02/L06/L19 on enlarged crops (AI model check only), used target L21 gloss (y su bi vn gia) for 20=gi and n_br=y, and proposed target-inferred codes (fa, fi, fo, 96, 99; bracketed in reading_2854.md), leaving 1 token {oo?} unresolved.

Located Mikel García Larragan's 16 July 2026 full online decipherment of #2854 alongside Tomokiyo (2018 §2.4), Bertomeu (pp. 212-213), and Ansorena (2017 lot 503), setting outcome.method='read from existing decipherment' and first_break=false; verified decrypt.py (1,914/1,915 = 99.95% across 126 types) and validate.py (LM/ch=-2.1317, z=+7.82 keys / +45.38 streams, p=0.0050, PASS; all-'e' and all-'a' negative controls FAIL exit 1).

Bracketed the 4 model-settled scan-amendment words (L03 [supiera], L45 [uuestra] [alteza], L62 [seruicio]) and all 15 words from codes inferred on #2854 alone (fa, fi, fo, 96, 99) in reading_2854.md and translation_2854.md: word_audit.py & v10_relabel.py measure 656/770 sure cipher words (read_share = 0.852, 114 explicit holes) -> read in part (Status: no write-up).

texts.label: AHPZ C_CRAR/000001/0024 (catalogue 2854, King Ferdinand II -> King John II, Seville, 9 June 1478)
texts.summary: In a 63-line royal cipher dispatch from Seville on 9 June 1478 (21 days before Prince Juan's birth), King Ferdinand II reports to his 79-year-old father King John II on King Ferrante I of Naples's proposal to hold French-occupied Roussillon and Cerdagne in escrow while auditing Louis XI's debt claims (while Ferdinand pursues parallel direct talks with France), endorses the Infante's lieutenancy, questions John II's recall of the Count of Cardona from Sardinia to Sicily, and warns that Viceroy Nicolás Carroz de Arborea is secretly negotiating to marry his daughter to rebel Marquis Leonardo de Alagón's eldest son so that the two would remain lords of Sardinia.

outcome.notes: Recorded as outcome.method='read from existing decipherment' and Status: no write-up because Mikel García Larragan published a full online decipherment of this letter on 16 July 2026 in a key family already published by Larragan and Tomokiyo (2018, §2.4). Our key (key_ferdinand1478.tsv) was independently rebuilt from sibling AHPZ C_CRAR/000001/0022 in the same file; strict v10 read_share = 656/770 = 0.852 (114 holes, read in part). Catalogue 2856 (C_CRAR/000001/0020) is reported separately in issue #1016.
